constraints: All forwarded candidates from the selected scorer run remain visible; the clinical stage only changes review priority or formal-pick status.
An imaging mention is episode context and never microbiological confirmation.
A differential-diagnosis imaging mention can promote an analytically credible opportunistic candidate to high-priority review, but never to Picked.
Host risk can promote an analytically credible opportunistic candidate to high-priority review, but never proves the organism.
Phenotype evidence is attached for review but has no deterministic effect while patient/event linkage remains provisional.
WBC, CRP, treatment response, and outcome are not used to attribute a specific pathogen.
Hospital-only genus, group, complex, spp., evidence, or pending-identification labels cannot be formal Picked species.
No patient is forced to have a Picked candidate.
The policy is answer blind; benchmark answers are used only by a separate post-hoc evaluator.
